items.stem: What does deduplication let the engine do?

options.text: Delete duplicate rows from the source system
Match a 'new' (unmapped) source record to an existing destination record and merge, instead of creating a duplicate
Skip every record that has a mapping
Compress the StarBridge database

items.explanation: Dedup catches records that have no mapping yet but already exist in the destination, linking and merging rather than duplicating.

misconceptions.a: Dedup acts on the destination side via the duplication key; it doesn't edit the source.

items.stem: When does deduplication run for a record?

options.text: On every record, every run
Only when the record has no existing mapping (an insert)
Only during GarbageCollection segments
Only when an exception is thrown

items.explanation: Dedup only applies to unmapped records. If a mapping already exists, the engine uses the fast mapping lookup instead.

misconceptions.a: Mapped records skip dedup — they're matched by their stored link.

items.stem: An unmapped source record is checked against the destination using its [DuplicationKey]. A match is found, and the source and destination field values are identical. What outcome results?

options.text: NewEntityCreated
DuplicateDetectedNoChangesMerged
DuplicateDetectedChangesMerged
Rejected

items.explanation: A duplicate was found and a mapping created, but since the values already matched, nothing needed merging: DuplicateDetectedNoChangesMerged.

misconceptions.c: That outcome is when the matched values differ and a delta is merged.
misconceptions.a: A match was found, so it is not created as new.

items.stem: What happens when dedup finds the record only *might* match an existing one (multiple candidate duplicates)?

options.text: It picks the first candidate automatically
It is referred for manual deduplication (a human decides)
It throws an exception
It creates a new record and ignores the candidates

items.explanation: Ambiguous matches are routed to ReferredForManualDeduplication so a person can resolve them, rather than guessing.

misconceptions.a: Auto-picking could merge the wrong records; the engine defers to a human instead.

items.stem: Why is deduplication important when one destination entity (e.g. Staff) is fed by multiple source systems?

options.text: It isn't relevant to multi-source entities
Without it, the second source would re-create records the first source already made, duplicating them
It lets each source have its own destination table
It disables change detection for shared entities

items.explanation: Multiple sources (via [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers]) converge on the same destination records; dedup matches them to existing records instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: Deduplication sits between the [DuplicationKey] attribute (L1.9) and mapping (L1.6). Explain how a successful dedup connects those two concepts.
rubric: Starts from L1.9: the [DuplicationKey] property is what the engine matches on (since no mapping exists yet)
Ends at L1.6: a successful match creates a new mapping linking the source ID to the matched destination record
Consequence: subsequent runs use the mapping lookup, not dedup
items.sampleAnswer: Because the record has no mapping, the engine matches on the field marked [DuplicationKey] (L1.9). When it finds the existing destination record, it creates a mapping (L1.6) to it and merges. From then on the record is mapped, so future runs use the direct mapping lookup and skip dedup entirely.
